title: ICJ Commences Oral Hearings on Guyana–Venezuela Essequibo Territorial Dispute
detail: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) began week-long public oral hearings at the Peace Palace in The Hague on May 4, 2026, on the merits of the border dispute between Guyana and Venezuela over the 160,000 km² Essequibo region — a territory Guyana administers but Venezuela claims as its own. Guyana opened proceedings on May 4 with oral arguments in two sessions (10:00–13:00 and 15:00–18:00), with Venezuela scheduled to present its arguments on May 6. The case, brought by Guyana, concerns the validity of the October 3, 1899 Arbitral Award that set the boundary. The Essequibo region is rich in gold, diamonds, and timber, and lies adjacent to massive offshore oil deposits discovered by ExxonMobil. The hearings coincided with renewed diplomatic tensions after Acting President Delcy Rodríguez of Venezuela was photographed on April 27–28 wearing a gold brooch depicting Venezuela's map including the Essequibo, prompting a formal protest from Guyana's President Irfaan Ali.
